# Purpose
Document the `R/sales_analysis.R` script and demonstrate transparent, reproducible analysis using synthetic retail orders.

## Inputs
The script generates 120 synthetic records internally. Each has an order ID, month, category, units, unit price, and calculated revenue. There are no external datasets or personal records.

## Process
1. Fix the random seed for reproducibility.
2. Generate sample order quantities and prices.
3. Compute revenue as units multiplied by unit price.
4. Aggregate revenue by month and category.
5. Check summary totals against raw totals.
6. Export CSV files and a PNG chart.

## Run the analysis
The setup chunk sets the working directory to the repository root when the report is knitted from `docs/`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
```

```{r run-analysis, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
source("R/sales_analysis.R")
```

## Preview the first records
```{r preview-orders}
head(orders)
```

## Summary tables
```{r summaries}
knitr::kable(monthly, caption = "Monthly synthetic revenue")
knitr::kable(category_totals, caption = "Revenue by category")
```

## Chart
```{r monthly-chart, fig.cap="Synthetic monthly revenue", echo=TRUE}
barplot(monthly$revenue, names.arg = as.character(monthly$month),
        col = "steelblue", main = "Monthly Revenue (Synthetic Data)",
        xlab = "Month", ylab = "Revenue (CAD)")
```

## Verification
```{r checks}
stopifnot(nrow(orders) == 120)
stopifnot(sum(monthly$revenue) == sum(orders$revenue))
stopifnot(sum(category_totals$revenue) == sum(orders$revenue))
# Independent check by summing the order-level values directly:
manual_formula_check <- sum(orders$units * orders$unit_price)
stopifnot(manual_formula_check == sum(orders$revenue))
```

## Outputs
The script writes `monthly_revenue.csv`, `category_revenue.csv`, and `monthly_revenue.png` to `outputs/`. R Markdown also renders this explanatory report to HTML.

## Limitations and ethical considerations
The synthetic records are illustrative only. Results must not be presented as actual sales. AI assistance was used for documentation and code scaffolding; the student is responsible for independently running, checking, and validating all results.
